feature: Ask animates a thing from general motion techniques
summary: Ask now picks from thirteen general motion techniques (turn on a pivot, fold over an edge, squash and stretch, throw on an arc, shake, pulse, sway in a chain, spin or orbit, draw a line on, pop in or out, enter or leave the frame, rest between laps, follow through and stagger) and its design says which one each moving part uses. Measured on a new sealed set of 16 everyday requests it has not yet moved the score: 38.6 before, 37.3 with what shipped.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open the New window (File > New), type: make an animated icon of a flag waving in the wind on its pole, and press Create.
Wait for Ask to finish, then press Space to play it. The flag is three strips, each swaying a little behind the last.
On an empty 512 by 512 picture press Command K and ask: make an animated icon of a door that swings open and closes again.
Press Space, and watch how the door moves (it turns flat about its corner, see rough).
On another empty picture press Command K and ask: make an animated icon of a cup of coffee with steam rising from it.
Choose Copy SVG and paste it into a browser: it plays as on the canvas.
Open the sealed set's sixteen results: .ask-eval/held-out-runs/20261115-030729-ask-held-out-motion/contact-sheet.png, and its best four then worst four as one video, ends-reel.mp4 in the same folder.

evaluate: Does the flag read as waving, or as three tiles wobbling apart?
Is a door that turns flat about its corner (rather than folding on its hinge edge) the first thing you would want fixed?
Does the steam's long rest after it fades read as a calm loop, or as the icon stopping?
Looking at the sealed set's sheet, is the weakness mostly the drawing or mostly the motion?
Is the catalogue in docs/design/ask.md the right set of techniques, or is one missing?
rough: Not done: the sealed set reads 37.3 against 38.6 before, after 3 of the 8 passes (pass 1 35.8, pass 3 34.1 reverted); the bar is 75. The task stays open for the next passes.
The door picked turn on a pivot instead of fold over an edge, so it swings flat like a clock hand and off the frame: choosing between those two is the next pass's lever.

A buzz the model made as one 0.2 s burst in a 2 s lap reads as still both to Ask's own look (12 frames a lap) and to the walk's check; the phone walk was swapped for steam, and the burst length is a next pass lever.
The flag's strips part at their seams while they sway: the chain is drawn as separate boxes, not one cloth.
The existing held-out animated group (h1 to h8) was not re-read this session: a whole held-out run is about 110 minutes and is due when the passes stop. Its last reading is 31.1 (2026-11-13).
The sealed set's sheet and reel stay in .ask-eval/held-out-runs, not in queue/audits, because the set is still being climbed on and every runner reads queue/audits (README, The held-out set).
The sheet shows 16 frames across each lap rather than two a beat: the eval films a lap evenly and does not know where a case's beats fall.
No mock covers what Ask draws, so there is no side by side with a mock.
